title: ci: add artifact signing, SBOM & provenance manifests for private-installer releases
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: Add end-to-end signing, SBOM generation, and provenance manifests to the private-installer release pipeline so customers can verify artifact integrity for VPC/on-prem installs. This PR wires artifact signing (cosign), generates SPDX SBOMs for installer images, produces machine-readable provenance manifests (release-manifest.yaml + provenance/<artifact>-provenance.json), and updates release automation to publish signatures and provenance to the secure release bucket.

Changes include: automated cosign signing and verification steps in the release pipeline, a lightweight provenance generator that records artifact SHA256 checksums, build environment metadata, and SLSA-like attestations, and updates to the Helm chart release packaging to include checksums in the chart artifact index. The Terraform module used by the release infra is updated to add object ACL restrictions and a lifecycle rule for provenance retention. Documentation and a new smoke-test that validates signature verification are included.

Checklist: 
- [x] CI: sign builder images with cosign (key stored in KMS, ephemeral key fetch during pipeline)
- [x] CI: generate SPDX SBOM for installer images and include in release bundle
- [x] CI: produce provenance JSON files with build metadata and checksums
- [x] Release automation: publish .sig and provenance JSON alongside tarballs and Helm charts
- [x] Terraform: add bucket ACL/policy adjustments for provenance objects
- [x] Docs: release/provenance.md with verification instructions
- [x] Tests: add pipeline smoke-test to verify cosign signatures and SBOM presence

Notes and constraints: we rely on cosign (OCI-based signatures) for installer container images and GPG-signed tarballs for legacy workflows; the release pipeline normalizes both into provenance manifests that reference both signature types. Keys are rotated using the existing key-rotation job (ENG-4209) and the CI fetches public keys from the secrets service at runtime. To avoid changing customer-facing artifact names we keep artifact filenames stable and publish additional files alongside (artifact.tar.gz, artifact.tar.gz.sig, artifact.tar.gz.sbom.json, artifact-provenance.json).

Security considerations: the provenance files are signed and stored in the release bucket with tighter ACLs; Terraform changes lock down write access to the provenance prefix and add an object-lock lifecycle rule to retain provenance for 90 days by default. The pipeline runs signature verification as a gating step before the release job completes.

Migration: Release automation consumers should continue to use the existing release index but can optionally consume provenance manifests for automated verification. The documentation includes example cosign verify commands and a short Go helper (scripts/release/verify-signatures.go) for automation.

Related: ENG-4821 (release hardening), SEC-133 (signing policy).
